title: At-will relationships and reliance loss
summary: A relationship that either party may end can still produce a separate reliance injury when a specific assurance induces the other party to give up an identifiable opportunity.
notes:
D&G Stout does not convert the distributorship into a permanent relationship. Its reasoning distinguishes anticipated future profits from the lost opportunity to sell the business on previously available terms. The appellate decision permits the claim to proceed; the later trial result is reported separately. Identify the exact assurance and the opportunity surrendered, rather than treating every disappointment following termination as compensable reliance.

D&G Stout separates a concrete sale opportunity forgone from income hoped for over an undefined future period. Its comparison to at-will employment distinguishes moving costs and old wages forgone in preparing to move from new wages expected after employment begins. The court leaves reasonable timing and proof for trial and does not convert the relationship into permanent employment or distribution.
